exposure: mode of presentation (abdominal mass, abdominal pain)
outcome: histopathological subtypes (mature teratomas, immature teratomas, yolk sac tumour, dysgerminomas, carcinoid tumour)
cohort: The study involved 86 ovarian specimens, of which 25 were germ cell tumours, from patients presenting to the Department of Pathology, Sree Balaji Medical College, Hospital and Research Institute, Chromepet, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India.
finding: Benign cystic teratomas were the most common ovarian germ cell tumours, primarily diagnosed between 21 and 40 years of age and presenting with abdominal pain and abdominal mass.
cross-section timing: Data collected from ovarian specimens and clinical records at the time of diagnosis and surgery.
